extraction.name: Geometry3K / Inter-GPS
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark of 3,002 high-school geometry problems with dense formal-language annotations, collected from two high-school textbooks and used to evaluate interpretable geometry problem solving with symbolic reasoning.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collected each problem from two popular high-school textbooks via two online digital libraries, including the problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer. Each problem was also annotated with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes, and dense formal-language descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Geometry problems from two high-school textbooks accessed through McGraw-Hill and Geometryonline; each item includes problem text, diagram image, four candidate choices, and correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was divided into train, validation, and test sets with a 0.7:0.1:0.2 ratio. For human-performance evaluation, test-split data were pushed to Amazon Mechanical Turk and annotators who did not meet the time/effort requirements were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem was annotated with dense formal-language descriptions, including unified structural descriptions for the problem text and diagram, as well as labels for the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No theorem application sequences were annotated due to worker labor; instead, 1,501 training samples with pseudo-optimal theorem application sequences were generated by random sampling and selecting positive sequences with minimum length.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators for dataset collection had undergraduate degrees. For human-performance evaluation, eligible annotators had a high school or higher degree; dozens of graduates majoring in science or engineering were also used as human experts.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hough Transformation, RetinaNet, MathPix, regular expressions, BART
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Education level; academic major (science or engineering) for human experts.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work may inspire research in symbolic reasoning and interpretable models and facilitate education.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is collected from high-school textbooks and covers grades 6-12, so it is centered on textbook-style SAT geometry problems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that less than 1% of problems can be solved without the diagram, and failure cases include inaccurate parsing, ambiguous annotations, multiple primitives, nested expressions, uncertain references, and an incomplete theorem set. The dataset is limited to high-school geometry problems from textbooks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, testing, and benchmarking of geometry problem solving systems; also used to train and evaluate problem parsers and symbolic reasoning models.
